headline: Boat Transfers and Coastal Permits for Mingan Archipelago
reservation: A national park entry pass is required, but the primary bottleneck is the private boat transport needed to reach the islands. Visitors must book water taxis or guided excursions directly with certified maritime operators departing from Havre-Saint-Pierre or Longue-Pointe-de-Mingan. Camping on the islands requires a specific permit and must be reserved through the Parks Canada reservation system well in advance.

days.title: Monoliths of the Western Sector

stops.name: Île aux Perroquets
stops.detail: Visit the historic lighthouse and observe the Atlantic Puffins that nest on the cliffs during the summer months.

stops.name: Île Nue de Mingan
stops.detail: Walk the tundra-like landscape to see stark limestone monoliths and unique flora adapted to the harsh maritime climate.

days.driving: Local boat transfer: 30–60 minutes; subject to sea conditions and fog.
days.note: Puffin sightings are most frequent from June through early August; bring binoculars for respectful viewing.

days.title: Giant Sculptures of the Central Islands

stops.name: Île Niapiskau
stops.detail: Discover the famous 'Madame de Niapiskau' monolith and explore the fossil-rich limestone formations along the shoreline.

stops.name: Île Quarry
stops.detail: Hike the diverse trails through boreal forest, bogs, and cliffs to see the largest concentration of erosion-formed sculptures.

days.driving: Local boat transfer: 45 minutes; allow time for safety briefings at the marina.
days.note: Trails on Île Quarry involve boardwalks; stay on the path to protect the sensitive arctic-alpine plants.

days.title: Mainland Interpretive Coastline

stops.name: Portage Trail (Mainland)
stops.detail: Explore the shoreline near the interpretation center to understand the geological forces that created the archipelago.

stops.name: Mingan Reception and Interpretation Centre
stops.detail: Engage with exhibits on the Ekuanitshit Innu culture and the biological diversity of the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; Route 138 is a paved but remote highway along the North Shore.
days.note: This is a mainland alternative if high winds or sea conditions prevent boat departures to the islands.

intel.title: Marina Staging
intel.text: Designated parking lots are available at the marinas in Havre-Saint-Pierre and Longue-Pointe-de-Mingan. These lots are intended for day-trippers; campers should check for long-term designated zones.

intel.title: Island Isolation
intel.text: Cellular signal is weak to non-existent on most islands in the archipelago. Maritime radios are the primary form of communication for boat operators; ensure your return pickup is confirmed.

intel.title: Route 138 Strategy
intel.text: Fuel stations are spaced significantly apart along the Côte-Nord. Always refill in Sept-Îles or Havre-Saint-Pierre before exploring the eastern reaches of the highway.

intel.title: Tide Dependent Exploration
intel.text: Access to many monoliths and sea caves is dependent on low tide. Consult the daily tide charts provided at the visitor center before departing for the islands to ensure safe beach walking.

intel.title: Maritime Operator Booking
intel.text: Parks Canada does not provide the boat transport; you must book with private 'Maritime Transport' partners. Schedules are highly weather-dependent and departures may be cancelled in high winds.

plan.arrival: Fly into Havre-Saint-Pierre or drive from Sept-Îles; check in at the Parks Canada station immediately to confirm boat operator status.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for Route 138; no vehicles are permitted on the islands themselves.
plan.goldenHour: The 'Petite Île au Marteau' viewpoint provides a striking silhouette of limestone formations against the sunset during late summer.
